newsitem.title: USA: Georgia loses 80,000 jobs in January.
newsitem.headline: Georgia loses 80,000 jobs in January.

text.p: Georgia lost nearly 80,000 seasonal jobs in January, with employment declining to 3.52 million, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said.
"January is the worst month of the year for seasonal job losses," he said.
Retailers and service industries laid off temporary workers after the holiday shopping season, conciding with the seasonal downturn in the construction industry.
Retail lost 40,000 jobs, other services laid off 17,700 temporary workers and construction declined by 6,600 jobs, Poythress said.

"Despite the job losses in January, our economy remains stable and payroll employment is expected to increase agiain in the spring and continue to grow at a moderate pace throughout the year," he said.
Over the year, Georgia added 106,200 jobs, for a grwoth rate of 3.1 percent.
All seven major metropolitan areas lost jobs from December to January.
